entities.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
observations: Clinical diagnosis is supported by pelvic/lower abdominal pain plus cervical motion tenderness in a sexually active patient when pregnancy and surgical emergencies are excluded.
Mucopurulent cervical discharge and abnormal bleeding increase specificity but no single laboratory test is required to establish PID.

entities.name: Chlamydia trachomatis infection
observations: Nucleic acid amplification testing can identify cervical Chlamydia infection as an etiology or coexisting STI, but a positive result is not required to diagnose PID.

entities.name: Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection
observations: Nucleic acid amplification testing or culture can identify gonococcal infection, but pathogen detection is ancillary and does not confirm or exclude PID.
